_about: Measured cost/memory coefficients for nvalchemi-toolkit + FairChem UMA, used by plan_run.py. Every number is from a real run; see benchmark/uma_efficiency/README.md for the derivations. Recalibrate by re-running the efficiency matrix (run_efficiency_matrix.sh) and refitting (README.md, 'Recalibrating').

reference.system: Au-Pt fcc, a = 4.00 A, 500 atoms (5x5x5 conventional cells), 1200 K
reference.measured: 2026-09-24..30, efficiency matrix (500 atoms, widths 1/2/4) + follow-up (widths 8/12, 108/256/2048 atoms, checkpointing, compile), A100-SXM4-80GB; compiled MD (dynamic shapes) 2026-10-09/10; checkpointed memory refit to 28,728 atoms 2026-10-19

time_model._form: one batched step takes c1_ms_per_atom * (n0_atoms + width * (N_eff * sf + nw_atoms)) ms on the reference GPU: n0 = per-call overhead in atom-equivalents (amortized by batching), nw = per-walker overhead (not amortized), sf = size_scaling factor, applied to compiled runs only. Least-squares fit (relative error) to every A100-SXM cell of the efficiency matrix and its follow-up: 108-2048 atoms, widths 1-16.

time_model._relative: An entry with 'relative_to' reuses that class's fit with c1 multiplied by 'factor' (the measured steady-state ratio at the widths listed). Compiled MD was measured at 500 atoms only; plan_run.py applies the compiled large-graph size ramp (size_scaling) to it as well, which is conservative.

memory_model._form: peak reserved GiB = base_gib + per_walker_gib * A + per_walker_cross_gib * A * (width - 1), A = width * N_eff / 500 (memory is linear in atom count; no size ramp). The cross term is non-zero only for SGC-NPT, whose memory grows faster than linear in the number of walkers. budget_scale lowers the usable fraction of the card for families the fit under-predicts.

compiled_merged.source: turbo with dynamic shapes: NPT w1 2.90 GiB; per-walker slope from Kawasaki-NPT w1/w4 (2.87 / 11.2 GiB). Replaces the 2026-09 static-shape fit, whose recompiles inflated reserved memory

memory_model._knee_form: Checkpointed classes ('form': 'knee'): allocated = base + below x min(A, knee) + above x max(0, A - knee), A = batch atoms (width x N_eff), GiB per 1000 atoms; reserved = allocated x reserved_factor. Checkpointing recomputes activations in fixed-size edge chunks, so above ~2,200 atoms in the batch memory grows ~6x more slowly.

size_scaling._note: Applied to compiled per-atom TIME only: one large graph costs more per atom under compile (Kawasaki turbo: 79 ms/step for 2048 atoms x 1 vs 58 ms for 500 x 4). Memory has no size ramp: it is linear in atom count (measured 108-2048 atoms).

a100-pcie-40gb.note: hybrid measured 13.82 vs 12.61 s/block on SXM

compile_overhead_s._note: One-time cost per process of compiling (first-call compile plus the first block's extra time, beyond the uncompiled run's), A100-SXM4-80GB, 500 atoms; the planner spreads it over --n-blocks. A persistent TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR may shrink it on later runs (unmeasured).
